doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Predicting hits: Dion, Riders in the Sky, Doggie in the Window
summary: Dion and the Belmonts hits, Riders in the Sky with Vaughn, Patti Page's Doggie in the Window and Itsy Bitsy Bikini, and how you never know what will catch on.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Now you played with Dion and the Belmonts.
Yeah we did a lot of that stuff for them.
Yeah. At the time did you ever have a sense of, well that song we did today, I think that is probably going to catch on?

No. Well once in a while I would say well there’s a hit record you know. And sure enough it would be a hit. But with Dion, I never knew that. The first six records we made with him were like million sellers. “The Wanderer” and “Teenager in Love.” But when I was with Vaughn Monroe we made a recording of a tune called “Riders in the Sky.” It was a different kind of rhythm. It was [scats] with the guitars. It was made in Chicago. And when we played a one-nighter in Detroit a few days later Vaughn played it about three times that night. Because the people went bananas. They wanted to hear that song. And it was a big smash, like in one night.
You never quite know what’s going to catch the public’s ear.
No. You never know. Yeah. But in those days a hit record was a glorious thing to have, for an artist to find some — Patti Page had a thing called “Doggie in the Window.”
“How Much is that Doggie in the Window.”
Yeah, we made it in the last five minutes of a three hour session. So how do you know? I think Doc Severinsen was playing trumpet on it.
I mean I can just picture you going home and saying hey man, guess what we did today.
“Itzy Bitzy Teeny Weeny Yellow Polka Dot Bikini.” Oh my God. That was Brian Hyland, wasn’t it?
